---
title: Comparison
engine: julia
---

Julia has several macros for cutting boilerplate out of struct definitions. This page
compares Terse.jl with `Base.@kwdef`, [QuickTypes.jl][qt], [Parameters.jl][par], and
[ConcreteStructs.jl][cs].

## Feature Matrix

| Feature | `@kwdef` | [Quick&shy;Types][qt] | [Param&shy;eters][par] | [Concrete&shy;Structs][cs] | **Terse** |
|---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Concise syntax | | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ |
| Default values | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Keyword constructors | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ |
| Mutable structs | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Parametric types | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ ᵃ | ✓ |
| Abstract supertypes | | | | | ✓ |
| Whole hierarchy at once | | | | | ✓ |
| Nested hierarchies | | | | | ✓ |
| Per-type mutability | | | | | ✓ |
| Const fields | | | | | ✓ |
| Computed constructors | | | | | ✓ |
| Hidden fields | | | | | ✓ |
| Escape hatch | | | | | ✓ |
| Source lines | — | ~540 | ~670 | ~245 | ~280 |
| Dependencies | — | 2 ᵇ | 2 ᶜ | 0 | 0 |

<sub>ᵃ type parameters inferred automatically</sub><br>
<sub>ᵇ ConstructionBase, MacroTools</sub><br>
<sub>ᶜ OrderedCollections, UnPack</sub>

[qt]: https://github.com/cstjean/QuickTypes.jl
[par]: https://github.com/mauro3/Parameters.jl
[cs]: https://github.com/SciML/ConcreteStructs.jl

## Side by Side Examples

The same hierarchy written five ways: an abstract `Animal` with a `Cat` (default
`lives = 9`) and a mutable `Dog` with a const `name` field and a keyword argument.

### Terse.jl

```{julia}
using Terse

@types Animal > (
    Cat(lives::Int = 9),
    @mutable Dog(@const(name::String); pointy_ears::Bool = true)
)

Cat(), Dog("Rex")
```

### QuickTypes.jl

One type at a time; `@qmutable` has no const field support, so `Dog` falls back to plain
Julia.

```julia
abstract type Animal end

@qstruct Cat(lives::Int = 9) <: Animal

mutable struct Dog <: Animal
    const name::String
    pointy_ears::Bool
    Dog(name::String; pointy_ears::Bool = true) = new(name, pointy_ears)
end
```

### Parameters.jl

Block syntax; no const field support in `@with_kw`.

```julia
abstract type Animal end

@with_kw struct Cat <: Animal
    lives::Int = 9
end

mutable struct Dog <: Animal
    const name::String
    pointy_ears::Bool
    Dog(name::String; pointy_ears::Bool = true) = new(name, pointy_ears)
end
```

### Base.@kwdef

No extra dependencies; no const field support in `@kwdef`.

```julia
abstract type Animal end

Base.@kwdef struct Cat <: Animal
    lives::Int = 9
end

mutable struct Dog <: Animal
    const name::String
    pointy_ears::Bool
    Dog(name::String; pointy_ears::Bool = true) = new(name, pointy_ears)
end
```

### ConcreteStructs.jl

`@concrete` infers type parameters from untyped fields rather than generating
constructors, so defaults, keyword arguments, and const fields are all written by hand.

```julia
abstract type Animal end

@concrete struct Cat <: Animal
    lives
end
Cat() = Cat(9)

mutable struct Dog <: Animal
    const name::String
    pointy_ears::Bool
    Dog(name::String; pointy_ears::Bool = true) = new(name, pointy_ears)
end
```
